title: OPUS SANFRAN
tagline: Three deliveries, five stars, and one steep city with nowhere clean to hide
description: A procedural third-person action-driving run set across a dense San Francisco district. Walk the hills, enter parked cars or boost occupied traffic, carry three packages across a routed street graph, and survive an escalating police response while pedestrians, signals, civilian drivers, weather, and mission state keep moving around you.
features: Third-person on-foot exploration with sprinting and mouse-driven camera control
Enter, exit, drive, and steal vehicles from live traffic
Ten-street SF district with hills, Victorians, storefronts, pedestrians, signals, and overhead wires
Three-delivery pickup and drop-off run with routed objectives, HUD guidance, timing, penalties, completion, and restart
Escalating five-star heat system with multi-car police pursuit, arrest, evasion, and stolen cruisers
Deterministic procedural geometry, Canvas textures, shaders, wet surfaces, daylight, dusk, and marine fog

lineage.note: The run predates Mirage's clean-room seed procedure. Repository history begins from an empty root commit and preserves the user prompt, reference-bar commit, and build history, but a neutral seed digest and runner isolation record were not preserved; independence cannot be established.

prompt.text:
Build a third-person open-world driving-and-shooting game set in San Francisco, playable in the browser. Everything generated programmatically — no imported assets.

The quality bar is the GTA V screenshots in `reference/gtav/`. Look at them. That is the fidelity we are chasing: the lighting, the density of the street, the way asphalt and buildings and traffic read at street level. The city itself must be San Francisco, not Los Santos — steep hills, the grid draped over them, fog, Victorians, the bay. Judge our look against the screenshots; judge our content against San Francisco.

Decide the approach yourself. Divide the goal into the smallest pieces that can be improved and judged independently. For each important piece, fan out a builder and a separate critic with fresh context — the critic must not see the builder's reasoning.

Each critic inspects the real running output (screenshot it), compares it directly against the bar with a blind A/B when possible, identifies the single biggest remaining gap, and sends it back for another round. Keep looping on each piece until our output wins or I stop the run.

Maintain a simple live HTML progress page that shows the work evolving over time — current screenshots next to the bar, what each critic said, what round each piece is on.

Use subagents and ultracode.
prompt.note: The repository preserves the complete user build objective in PROMPT.md. Claude Code system instructions, developer instructions, and runner logs were not preserved, so the prompt is conservatively labeled partial.

licenses.assetStatement: The deployed runtime uses first-party procedural geometry, Canvas textures, shaders, interface graphics, and a first-party gameplay screenshot as its cover. Three.js 0.185.1 runtime code is bundled under MIT with its license retained. No third-party art, audio, fonts, models, maps, or textures ship in dist. The repository's development-only GTA V comparison screenshots are excluded from the deployment and are not game assets.

presentation.coverAlt: A black player car descends a dense San Francisco street at sunset between Victorian buildings, traffic, pedestrians, signals, storefronts, and overhead wires
controls: WASD to move on foot and drive
E to enter or exit the nearest vehicle
limitations: Desktop keyboard and mouse are the only tested input modes; touch and gamepad are not claimed.
No player shooting system or audio system is implemented; the action loop is walking, driving, vehicle theft, deliveries, and police pursuit.

The latest full keyboard harness passed 155 of 172 checks; timing and state-sequencing failures were concentrated in long-running traffic, possession carry-over, mission best-time, and police arrest or escape scenarios.
Long-running traffic and police behavior is nondeterministic and can stall or fail to close distance.
The storage-disabled Mirage sandbox cannot preserve best times across reloads, but the mission remains playable without storage.
Characters and vehicles use stylized procedural geometry rather than authored skeletal animation or photoreal materials.
